around.headline: Student accuses Bengaluru landlord of sexual harassment during a flat inspection
around.summary: A student has accused a Bengaluru landlord of hugging and kissing her during a flat inspection, and a complaint has been filed. If you are house-hunting, treat a viewing like meeting a stranger: don't go alone, and share the address and the owner's number with someone before you enter.

around.headline: Fake drugs worth Rs 5 crore seized in Bidadi; expired milk and curd found at Karnataka railway stations
around.summary: Enforcement teams seized counterfeit medicines worth about Rs 5 crore at Bidadi on Bengaluru's outskirts, while separate checks turned up expired curd and milk, and food packed in newspaper, at Karnataka railway stations. Buy medicines only from licensed chemists who give a printed bill, and skip loose dairy and newspaper-wrapped food at stations.

around.headline: ORR firms push to delay road works as morning jams stretch 13.5 km
around.summary: Companies along the Outer Ring Road want the white-topping works deferred after rush-hour jams stretched 13.5 km, and one founder posted photos of empty desks saying his 17-km commute took two hours. Nothing has been deferred yet, so plan ORR trips around the peaks rather than through them.
around.source: The News Minute, Deccan Herald, Business Today

around.headline: Varthur residents leave five hours early for flights; Sarjapur residents build their own carpool app
around.summary: East Bengaluru residents say they now leave up to five hours ahead to catch a flight, and a Sarjapur group has launched its own carpooling app rather than wait for a civic fix. If you fly out of KIA from the Varthur–Sarjapur belt, price in the airport run as a half-day, not an hour.

around.headline: Karnataka High Court protects 15 Bengaluru street vendors from eviction, seeks state report on vending zones
around.summary: The High Court has restrained authorities from evicting 15 Bengaluru street vendors and asked the state to report on designated vending zones. It is a reminder that licensed vendors have statutory protection — eviction drives have to follow the vending-zone process, not just clear a footpath.

around.headline: Sensex snaps a four-day losing streak, jumping 628 points; Nifty closes at 24,232
around.summary: Indian markets rebounded today, with the Sensex up 628 points and the Nifty ending at 24,232 after four straight sessions of losses. If you invest through SIPs, this is the kind of swing to ignore — the streak and the bounce are both within normal weekly noise.

around.headline: Southern chief ministers share a stage with Amit Shah; Tamil Nadu CM pushes a Bengaluru–Hosur metro link and Cauvery verdict compliance
around.summary: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay, Karnataka's D.K. Shivakumar and Andhra's Chandrababu Naidu appeared together at a meeting convened by Amit Shah, where Vijay pitched a Bengaluru–Hosur metro connection and urged the Centre and neighbouring states to follow the Supreme Court's Cauvery verdict. Both threads matter locally — one could eventually shape the commute to Hosur, the other decides how Bengaluru's water is shared.
around.source: Hindustan Times, Deccan Herald, DT Next

street_smart.title: A landlord agrees to show you the flat — but only when no one else is around. During the viewing he moves in close and touches you. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Today's real incident: a student has accused a Bengaluru landlord of hugging and kissing her during a flat inspection (The Times of India). Harassment during a property viewing has not been used as a scenario in the last three weeks of briefs.
street_smart.situation: You found the listing online, the broker didn't show up, and the owner insisted on a viewing at a time the building is empty. No one else knows exactly where you are.

choices.text: Leave the flat immediately, get to a public spot, and call 112 the same day — give the flat address and the owner's number, keep the listing screenshot and your chat, and file the complaint even if it means going to a station far from home.
choices.feedback: Correct, and the timing is the whole point. Unwanted physical contact is a cognizable offence under Section 74/75 of the BNS, and a Zero FIR means any police station has to register it regardless of which jurisdiction the flat falls in — so 'wrong station' is never a reason to postpone. A same-day complaint plus the listing and chat records ties a named person to a specific address and time, which is exactly what a later denial cannot survive.

choices.text: Say nothing, walk out quietly and just skip that flat — no one witnessed it, and chasing it will only eat your week.
choices.feedback: This is the mechanism the behaviour depends on. Someone who does this picks house-hunters precisely because they are strangers, in a hurry, often new to the city, and reliably decide the hassle isn't worth it — so the listing goes right back up and the next person walks into the same empty building. Your silence isn't neutral; it's the thing that keeps the setup working.

choices.text: Go back for a second viewing, this time with your phone recording, so you have hard proof before complaining.
choices.feedback: You would be deliberately re-entering an empty flat with someone who has already assaulted you, on the theory that better evidence is needed. It isn't — your own statement is evidence, and the police can seize his phone and the listing records. Escalation risk goes up sharply the second time, and courts do not require a victim to manufacture a repeat offence.

choices.text: Post his photo, number and the listing on a local WhatsApp or Reddit group first, so others are warned right away.
choices.feedback: The warning instinct is right, the order is wrong. Publishing before a complaint exists invites a defamation counter-case that flips you into defending yourself, and it tips him off to delete the listing and chats you would have relied on. File first, then warn — the complaint number makes the public post far harder to attack.

choices.text: Tell only the broker or the rental platform and ask to be shown a different flat.
choices.feedback: Worth doing, but not on its own. A broker's incentive is the commission on that building, and platforms typically delist quietly with no record that survives anywhere useful. Report it to them in writing by all means — after the police complaint, not instead of it.

takeaways: Never view a flat alone: take someone with you, or share live location plus the address and the owner's number with a friend before you go in.
The moment it turns physical, leave and call 112 (women's helpline 181, or 1091) — a Zero FIR can be registered at any police station, so jurisdiction is never a reason to wait.
Save the listing screenshot, the owner's or broker's number and every chat message the same day; deleted listings are the first thing that disappears.

quiz.question: How long did Bengaluru's Outer Ring Road morning jam stretch this week, prompting firms to ask for road works to be delayed?
quiz.why: The works in question are the Rs 450-crore white-topping project — resurfacing a road in concrete rather than asphalt, which lasts far longer but shuts lanes for months while it is laid.

quiz.question: Which pharma company's Bengaluru manufacturing unit did the US FDA clear this week, sending its shares up sharply?
quiz.why: The inspection closed with a 'VAI' outcome — Voluntary Action Indicated, meaning the FDA found issues but not serious enough to demand corrective action, which is why the market treated it as good news.

quiz.question: Where did the Nifty close today, as the Sensex snapped a four-day losing streak with a 628-point jump?
quiz.why: The Sensex and Nifty track different baskets — 30 companies on the BSE versus 50 on the NSE — which is why their point moves are never directly comparable.

quiz.question: The Cauvery, in the news again today over compliance with the Supreme Court's verdict, originates in which district?
quiz.why: It rises at Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri hills of Kodagu, and Bengaluru draws the bulk of its piped water from this river, pumped roughly 100 km uphill from Torekadanahalli.

quiz.question: What does a 'Zero FIR' let you do?
options: File a complaint without paying any fee
File an FIR at any police station, regardless of where the offence happened
quiz.why: The station registers it with number zero and transfers it to the right jurisdiction — introduced so that no complaint is lost to the delay of finding the 'correct' station, and refusing to register one is itself an offence for the officer.
